question: Does the candidate quality score used by the production quality floor (score >= 82) predict reaching TP1?
source: production PostgreSQL, read-only transaction (BEGIN READ ONLY ... ROLLBACK)
population: ml_rejected_signals shadow rows resolved to sl/tp1/tp2/tp3 in the last 60 days, one row per asset x timeframe x strategy x direction x bar (first logged)
metric: AUC of each feature for TP1-or-better, average ranks for ties (0.5 = no information)
conclusion: Score carries no measurable information about reaching TP1 (AUC 0.489, about 1.4 standard errors below 0.5 at n=6190). Candidates below the floor did not do worse.
limits: score is recorded only on 6,190 recent rows, 91% of them scored 90+
rows are candidates the ML gate rejected, so they are not a random sample of all candidates
an earlier draft used rank() without tie averaging and understated AUC; corrected here
action: none; replacing the floor is an owner decision
